Full suite re-run clean, no new failures beyond the 2 pre-existing conformance-fixture ones.  The text it replaced read: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-29: DamageCmd.deal (sts2_rl/cmds.py) still has no `target.is_dead` guard at entry -- only `should_allow_hitting(target)`, a pure listener aggregation (default True) unrelated to death state. A call against an already-dead target would still run modify_damage_additive/multiplicative/cap, on_attacked, before_damage_received and block absorption against it; only on_damage_received (step 9) is guarded. DORMANT, re-enumerated by execution rather than inherited: classified every `DamageCmd.deal(` call site with a script (34 sites sit inside a loop / are multi-hit or multi-target, 40 are single, unlooped calls) and read the loop sites. Every multi-hit-against-one-target site re-checks `target.is_gone` (which is `is_dead or escaped`) before each hit -- Twin Strike (cards/twin_strike.py:38), Fiend Fire (cards/fiend_fire.py:41), monster `_execute_attack` (monsters/base.py:136, checked AFTER each hit, before the next). CombatState.resolve_target and CombatState.enemy both walk the list for the first NOT-`is_gone` creature and only fall back to a possibly-dead `enemies[0]` when every enemy is already gone (a state combat should already have ended on). NUANCE not closed by this check: the AoE relics' `living_enemies()` is a snapshot taken ONCE before the loop, so a listener that kills a LATER-indexed enemy as a side effect of the FIRST hit (a chain-kill) would still be re-hit by this loop where C# would skip it -- no such chain-kill listener was found in the sim (checked: none of the six relics' own damage has any on-hit forwarding effect), so this residual is itself unreached. Checked against guard N1 (should_allow_hitting, the sim's own documented C#-has-no-single-hook-here divergence for reviving Decimillipede-style segments): a withered, retained segment (hp<=0, retained_after_death) is is_dead for the entire window it is unhittable, so the new guard alone reproduces that unhittable window too, redundantly with should_allow_hitting rather than in conflict with it -- no change to should_allow_hitting was made or needed. Re-checked every DamageCmd.deal call site the record's own G5 enumeration named (34 loop sites: monsters/base.py's _execute_attack, cards/whirlwind.py, the fixed-AoE relics) -- none constructs or relies on hitting an already-dead target, so the new guard changes no currently-observed behavior; it closes the structural absence only. TDD: test/test_hook_order.py::TestDamagePipelineOrder::test_dead_target_is_skipped_entirely_no_hooks_fire (RED before the fix: dealt==6 instead of 0 and every pipeline hook fired; GREEN after). Full suite re-run clean, no new failures beyond the 2 pre-existing conformance-fixture ones.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-29: the dealer-half is CLOSED. cmds.py's DamageCmd.deal now opens with `if dealer is not None and dealer.is_dead: return 0`, matching CreatureCmd.cs:242-245 exactly (spec step 1, re-verdicted `faithful` this pass). The target-half remains open: no `target.is_dead` guard exists at entry (spec step 3, kept `gap`/`live: false`). RE-ENUMERATED by execution rather than inherited: classified all `DamageCmd.deal(` call sites in sts2_rl/ (74 files, 34 inside a loop) and read every loop site. Every multi-hit-single-target site re-checks is_gone/is_dead between hits (Twin Strike, Fiend Fire, Sword Boomerang, monster `_execute_attack`); every all-enemies AoE site filters through `living_enemies()` (Whirlwind plus 6 fixed-AoE relics: Charon's Ashes, Festive Popper, Mercury Hourglass, Mr. Struggles, Screaming Flagon, Stone Calendar); `CombatState.resolve_target`/`.enemy` skip `is_gone` creatures and only fall back to a possibly-dead `enemies[0]` when every enemy is already gone. guards.what: N1: sim-only should_allow_hitting pre-check has no single C# analogue inside CreatureCmd.Damage
guards.rationale: C# excludes unhittable/reviving creatures upstream, via IsAlive-based target filtering in AttackCommand.GetPossibleTargets (AttackCommand.cs:544-546) plus real-death semantics for reviving Decimillipede-style segments, rather than a dedicated hook inside CreatureCmd.Damage itself. The sim's should_allow_hitting hook (used only by MockRevivePower/ReattachPower-family reviving-segment logic, sts2_rl/powers.py:1572-1575, 2354-2357, 3372-3375) re-architects this as an explicit pipeline predicate. Net effect is equivalent for the currently-ported content (Decimillipede); documented so a future audit doesn't mistake it for an unmapped C# hook.

guards.what: N2: DamageCmd.deal takes a single Creature per call; CreatureCmd.Damage batches IEnumerable<Creature> and defers all targets' step-17/18 events until every target in the call has resolved blocking/HP-loss
guards.rationale: The sim's callers (card code, Monster._execute_attack) loop over multiple simultaneous targets themselves, each a fully independent DamageCmd.deal call including its own Kill() processing, rather than the pipeline batching them. For a C# attack that hits several creatures at once, every target's AfterDamageGiven/AfterDamageReceived-or-skip resolves before ANY of them is actually Kill()'d; in the sim, the first target's entire pipeline (including death processing) completes before the second target's begins. No concretely broken current interaction was found (the one candidate, Decimillipede's ReattachPower 'are all other segments dead' check, is evaluated on a segment's own later turn, well after any same-turn AOE has already fully resolved in both architectures), but this is a real structural difference. Cross-reference: primarily the concern of the creature_card_cmds seam (Task 7), which owns how cards orchestrate multi-target attacks; recorded here because it originates in DamageCmd.deal's own signature.

guards.what: N3 (LIVE): additive/multiplicative dispatch is a parallel sum/product in the sim vs a sequential running-value chain in C# -- RAISED from deliberate-divergence to gap in the Task 9 fix pass
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: hooks.modify_damage_multiplicative is now a CHAIN, not a product -- it folds each listener's factor into the running amount and returns the new amount, exactly as ModifyDamageInternal does (`num *= item2.ModifyDamageMultiplicative(...)`, Hook.cs:2515-2538) -- and DamageCmd.deal applies the returned value directly. The block twin, hooks.modify_block_multiplicative, was changed the same way against Hook.ModifyBlock (Hook.cs:1310-1340), which closes the site creature_card_cmds step 13 carried. The recorded witness now agrees: Shrink (x0.7) plus Vulnerable (x1.5) on a 20-damage powered attack gives 20*1.5 = 30, 30*0.7 = 21. The strict xfail that pinned this (test_multiplicative_damage_modifiers_chain_sequentially) is gone from test/test_hook_order.py and the test passes. The additive family still hands every listener the same pre-step base rather than the running total, which is exactly equal over integers and was already settled on the merits. WAS: the sim multiplied every factor together in float and applied the product once, giving 20 where the game gives 21.

HookSystem._each runs a complete listener pass per suffix in the order _very_early, _early, plain, _late (sts2_rl/hooks.py), so hooks.should_die now makes a full plain pass before any Late one -- the shape Hook.ShouldDie has at Hook.cs:2229-2249.
